title: SOS origin-signature requirement unimplementable under hop-by-hop LLSec re-signing
description: Exposed by review of project-LICHEN-worker6-lzgc (all 3 passes flagged; pre-existing). spec/12-apps.md:707-709 requires SOS to 'carry a valid link-layer signature from the originating node ... verified at each receiving node before rebroadcast', but LLSec is hop-by-hop: relays create a new link frame, allocate their own replay counter, populate their own SIID and re-sign (spec/06-security.md:64-71 — 'Hop Limit changes never occur under an unchanged link signature'; spec/02-physical-link.md:305-308). No verbatim-forwarding exemption exists, so past hop 1 no receiver can verify an ORIGIN link signature. Decide: (a) add an SOS end-to-end origin signature object (DAO Origin Signature pattern, 06-security.md §8.6) carried in the SOS payload; or (b) re-scope the requirement to first-hop verification plus the (unauthenticated) preserved-source accounting of §6.3.3, stating the residual forgery ceiling. Until resolved, multi-hop SOS has no authenticated origin.
close_reason: Resolved with option (a), forced by settled §8.4 doctrine (end-to-end origin auth is a separate object; hop-by-hop LLSec cannot authenticate origin past hop 1) and by the already-implemented Python sos_origin.py / Rust sos_origin.rs / shared sos_signature.json vectors. Rewrote spec/12-apps.md §18.4.1 Authentication to require a 56-octet SOS Origin Signature (8B BE Origin Sequence + 48B Schnorr48) over SHA-512('LICHEN-SOS-ORIGIN-v1' || origin 02xx || seq || canonical CBOR payload), mirroring the DAO §8.6 pattern, with a per-origin monotonic replay gate; hop-by-hop LLSec still verified/re-signed per hop. Spec-only change (no code touched); verification = field-for-field match against both implementations + independent test-vector oracle. 3x codereview (correctness/security/edge-cases): PASS/PASS/PASS. Delegated reviewer (opencode run kimi-k3) timed out before verdict on 2 attempts (env); passes completed directly with same references.
